In time series forecasting, observations at times 1, 2, ..., k+i–1 are used to estimate the forecasting model. The error on the forecast for k+i is then computed. This step is repeated for i = 2,...,T–k where T is the total number of observations. The forecast accuracy over all errors is then computed. This procedure is sometimes known as a "rolling forecasting origin" because the "origin" (k+i -1) at which the forecast is based rolls forward in time. Further, two-step-ahead or in general p-step-ahead forecasts can be computed by first estimating the model using observations up to time k+i–p, and then using this model to forecast the value at time k+i.
